# semaphore_ex_project_ssh_key_policy (Resource)

Singleton policy owning the project default and always SSH key binding selections. Removing it clears only those two project fields.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "semaphore_ex_project" "dependencies" {
  name = "Private dependencies"
}

resource "semaphore_ex_project_generated_ssh_key" "dependencies" {
  project_id       = semaphore_ex_project.dependencies.id
  name             = "Dependency repositories"
  login            = "git"
  login_wo_version = 1
  algorithm        = "ed25519"
}

resource "semaphore_ex_project_ssh_key_policy" "dependencies" {
  project_id = semaphore_ex_project.dependencies.id
  default_ssh_keys = [{
    access_key_id = semaphore_ex_project_generated_ssh_key.dependencies.id
    hosts         = ["github.com", "gitlab.com"]
  }]
  always_ssh_keys = []
}

# Authorize the generated public key on your Git hosts.
# The separate policy allows keys and project to be created in the same apply.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (Number) Project owning this singleton policy.

### Optional

- `always_ssh_keys` (Attributes List) Keys added to every effective template or task selection. An empty list explicitly selects none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--always_ssh_keys))
- `default_ssh_keys` (Attributes List) Default selection inherited by templates and tasks that do not override it. An empty list explicitly selects none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_ssh_keys))

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The ID of this resource.

### Nested Schema for `always_ssh_keys`

Required:

- `access_key_id` (Number)

Optional:

- `hosts` (List of String) Optional exact lowercase DNS or IP host mapping; server validation decides when host routing is required.

### Nested Schema for `default_ssh_keys`

Optional:

- `hosts` (List of String) Optional exact lowercase DNS or IP host mapping; server validation decides when host routing is required.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import the singleton policy using its project ID.
terraform import semaphore_ex_project_ssh_key_policy.dependencies 1
```
